title: a-ticket-can-be-sent-back-to-fixme
intention: The workflow grammar knows FIXME ("fix my design"): a ticket can be sent back into FIXME carrying the list of what it is missing, and it cannot leave FIXME for BUILDME while any missing item is unanswered on the ticket.
why: Akien, verbatim (relayed in ~/.cairn/foreground-decisions.md item 1, 2026-10-01): "whoever asked is the ticket itself. recording the refusal is not important to furthering anything. yes it becomes open work. But where?" / "it becomes open work in deisgn. it goes back to ticketing for improvement." / "FIXME. that's approved thru PROVED"
traces_to: Law 9 and Law 4: a refused crossing is a red, and the red's only legal motion is back to design; today the refusal is an exception string plus a trouble the ticket never sees, so nothing in the ticket's own state says it is broken. The 2026-08-10 ruling decisions/2026-08-10-the-ticket-owns-the-refusal: "the gate is the refuser but it's doing so on behalf of the ticket. so the ticket owns the refusal." / "the ticket owns the workflow".
how: code-seam v2 in CairnCommons/node_classes/code-seam.json gains `repair_summons: ["FIXME"]`; cairn/tools/base/transitions.py reads it: a back-edge into FIXME from BUILDME or later inserts FIXME immediately before BUILDME (or re-enters it when already present), _conform lifts it out of the backbone the way it lifts free summonses, and the forward crossing FIXME -> BUILDME runs a FIXME exit gate that reads the ticket off disk and refuses while any entry of its `fixme` list has no decision whose step is `FIXME <n>`. Proved by cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_fixme.py.
falsifier: RED if over fixture tickets: (1) a back-edge into FIXME from PROVEME does not land at FIXME placed before BUILDME with the missing list journaled on the crossing; (2) the forward crossing FIXME -> BUILDME is not refused while any `fixme` entry has no `FIXME <n>` decision; (3) it is refused once every entry is answered; (4) a v2 string without FIXME stops conforming or changes its legal targets. Horizon: the tester seal.
watchme: none, because the first consumer is the harbor_master sibling ticket, whose clearance refusal in cairn/devices/cairn/machines/harbor_master/clearance.py sends real boats into FIXME; a FIXME that cannot be left or entered shows there as a refused crossing at that ticket's own PROVED
children: none, because the change is one declaration in CairnCommons/node_classes/code-seam.json and its reader in cairn/tools/base/transitions.py
builder_notes: A Haiku builder would ask: (1) Where is FIXME declared? code-seam.json workflow_versions.v2 gains "repair_summons": {"FIXME": "BUILDME"} — the value is the backbone state FIXME sits immediately before. (2) How does _conform treat it? Lifted out of the backbone with free summonses and dispositions; it may occur at most once and only directly before its anchor, else MalformedWorkflow. (3) How does a ticket enter it? emit(wf, 'FIXME', ...) when FIXME is absent and the cursor is at or after the anchor: the workflow is first rewritten with FIXME inserted before the anchor (cursor shifted by one), then the move is an ordinary back-edge (ungated, severity carried); when FIXME is present it is an ordinary earlier summons. Entering FIXME requires a non-empty list `missing` on the crossing, else IllegalTransition. (4) The exit gate? A forward crossing out of FIXME runs FIXME_GATE = TransitionGate('fixme_gate', exception_class=FixmeGateRed): it reads the ticket named on the crossing via _find_ticket and refuses unless its `fixme` field is a non-empty list and every entry n (1-based) has a decision with step 'FIXME <n>' and non-empty text. (5) Proof? cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_fixme.py over a temp node-class root and a temp _TICKETS dir, one tooth per falsifier clause.

chart_claim.filled_by: CC chart chain (orient fe26250bc0c8 .. validate 36cf232980dd, each learned)

decisions.text: STEP 1, the red proof, measured 2026-10-01. Write cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_fixme.py, run as a script through print_teeth_main(__file__) from cairn.tools.proof_coverage (discovers test_* functions). Fixtures: a node-class root = scratch_dir('fixme_fixture_node_classes_') holding a copy of the live CairnCommons/node_classes/code-seam.json whose workflow_versions.v2 gains 'repair_summons': {'FIXME': 'BUILDME'} (set in the copy, so the proof does not depend on the live write); a ticket corpus repointed the way test_emission_gate.py's _Corpus does (save transitions._TICKETS, set it to a scratch_dir holding <name>.json, restore in finally); a component address = scratch_dir(...)/comp with history.json/state.json paths passed to emit (nested one level, as test_emission_gate's _cross explains). Resolve emit, parse_workflow, legal_targets, load_class_def and FixmeGateRed from cairn.tools.base.transitions INSIDE each tooth, so a reverted build reds teeth instead of crashing the import. Teeth: test_a_back_edge_lands_at_fixme_before_buildme (emit('code-seam@v2: THINKME -> TICKETME -> BUILDME -> [PROVEME] -> PROVED', 'FIXME', history_path, state_path, node_class_root=root, ticket=name, missing=['the receiver is unnamed']): parse_workflow(new).here == 'FIXME', its path index is path.index('BUILDME') - 1, and the last history entry's 'missing' equals the list); test_fixme_refuses_exit_while_an_entry_is_unanswered (fixture ticket with fixme=['a','b'] and decisions=[{'step':'FIXME 1','text':'answered'}]: emit of the FIXME-carrying string at [FIXME] to 'BUILDME' with ticket=name raises FixmeGateRed); test_fixme_admits_exit_once_every_entry_is_answered (decisions for FIXME 1 and FIXME 2 with text: transitions._fixme_gate(name) returns (note, record) without raising — called directly because the BUILDME entry gate behind it reds any fixture ticket that has no chart); test_a_v2_string_without_fixme_is_unchanged (for every cursor position of the plain v2 path, legal_targets under the fixture class def equals legal_targets under a deepcopy with repair_summons removed, and both conform). PROVES = {'72d2f79daf0a': {'1': 'test_a_back_edge_lands_at_fixme_before_buildme', '2': 'test_fixme_refuses_exit_while_an_entry_is_unanswered', '3': 'test_fixme_admits_exit_once_every_entry_is_answered', '4': 'test_a_v2_string_without_fixme_is_unchanged'}}. Run red: teeth 1-3 fail (FIXME is not in the vocabulary / no _fixme_gate); tooth 4 may pass before the build, which is expected.

STEP 2, the declaration. The value is the DICT form {'FIXME': 'BUILDME'} (builder_notes (1)); the how's list form ['FIXME'] is superseded by this decision, because the anchor is a fact the grammar needs and a list cannot carry it. Write it into the live CairnCommons/node_classes/code-seam.json under workflow_versions.v2 as 'repair_summons': {'FIXME': 'BUILDME'} through the artifact door: a scratchpad .py that loads the JSON, sets the key, and calls cairn.tools.artifact.artifact.write(path, json.dumps(doc, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False) + '\n', verb='cast', why='72d2f79daf0a: code-seam v2 declares FIXME as a repair summons anchored before BUILDME (Akien 2026-10-01, foreground item 1: no migration, no ticket is at FIXME)'). Match the file's existing indent (read it first and keep it). Akien approved adding FIXME to v2 in place: no ticket stands at FIXME, so no instance changes shape.

STEP 3, the build in cairn/tools/base/transitions.py, measured 2026-10-01 (Workflow is a frozen dataclass at line 533; _conform at 639; emit at 1875; gates declared at 1055-1059). (a) class FixmeGateRed(IllegalTransition) beside the other *Red classes; FIXME_GATE = TransitionGate('fixme_gate', exception_class=FixmeGateRed) beside the other gates. (b) _conform: repair = reg.get('repair_summons', {}); for each state, anchor in repair.items(): hits = positions of state in wf.path; more than one -> MalformedWorkflow naming it; one hit whose next state is not anchor -> MalformedWorkflow naming the anchor; the backbone comprehension also drops states in repair. (c) emit, right after canon_target: reg = _registered_workflow(class_def, wf.version); repair = reg.get('repair_summons', {}); target = canon(target, list(repair)) or target; if target in repair and target not in wf.path: a = wf.path.index(repair[target]); if wf.cursor < a raise IllegalTransition(f'{target} is entered from {repair[target]} or later'); pad objects to len(path) with None, then wf = dataclasses.replace(wf, path=wf.path[:a] + (target,) + wf.path[a:], objects=objs[:a] + (None,) + objs[a:], cursor=wf.cursor + 1). Then, if target in repair and resolve_target(wf, target) < wf.cursor: missing = journal_extra.get('missing'); unless it is a non-empty list of non-empty str raise IllegalTransition('entering FIXME needs missing=[...] — the list of what the design lacks'). Validation, render and the back-edge record then proceed unchanged, and journal_extra carries missing into the record. (d) inspect_fixme(ticket) -> list[dict]: one _lane('every_fixme_entry_is_answered', expected='every fixme entry 1..N has a decision with step FIXME <n> and non-empty text', actual= the same string when true, else a string naming the ticket-not-found, the empty/absent fixme list, or the unanswered entry numbers, code='transitions.py::inspect_fixme', ticket=ticket, unanswered=[...]). It reads the ticket via _find_ticket(ticket) (None ticket or no file is a red, never a pass). _fixme_gate(ticket) = FIXME_GATE.run(inspect_fixme(ticket), note=None). (e) In emit's gated branch, BEFORE the 'if target == "BUILDME"' entry block: if wf.here in repair and target_idx > wf.cursor: fixme_note, _rec = _fixme_gate(journal_extra.get('ticket')); proved += _rec; and the record gains **({'fixme_gate': fixme_note} if fixme_note else {}). Import dataclasses and canon (canon is already imported for canon_target; check) at module top. Run test_fixme.py green twice, then run cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_emission_gate.py and test_transitions*.py in cairn/tools/base/proofs to confirm no other tooth moved.

D3(e)'s target_idx is emit's existing local, measured 2026-10-01 at cairn/tools/base/transitions.py:1915: target_idx = resolve_target(wf, target), computed in the gated branch before every gate check (lines 1940-2061 all read it). The FIXME block is written after that line and after the FIXME insertion of (c), so it reads the same local; it computes nothing new.

D1's fixture utility is from cairn.devices.tester.scratch import scratch_dir (scratch_dir(prefix) returns a fresh Path under the tester's scratch root); transitions is from cairn.tools.base import transitions. Both are already the imports of the built and sealed cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_fixme.py (lines 38-39), so D1 is satisfied as written; no tempfile substitute.
